piece.title: String Quartet in C major, Hob.III:77, Op.76 No.3 (“Emperor”)
piece.why: Easy hero: Haydn's “Emperor” hymn, melody in Violin I over a clean four-part chorale accompaniment.

plan.summary: As written (no arranging): the original parts are handed out unchanged. The source parts in score order (Violin 1, Violin 2, Viola and Violoncello) are paired with the players sorted from highest to lowest range center (the midpoint of each player's sounding range): Violin 1 → Flute; Violin 2 → Clarinet in B♭; Viola → Alto Sax in E♭; Violoncello → Bassoon. No octave shifts, no chord changes beyond what a one-note instrument requires (a wind or brass player plays the top note of a double stop or chord), and no repair: a note outside a player's range stays where it is and is marked with an x notehead.

assignments.reason: as written: Violin 1 goes to Flute, the highest range center (sounding D4–G6); no octave shift, no repair
as written: Violin 2 goes to Clarinet in B♭, the 2nd highest range center (sounding D3–B♭5); no octave shift, no repair
as written: Viola goes to Alto Sax in E♭, the 3rd highest range center (sounding E♭3–G5); no octave shift, no repair
as written: Violoncello goes to Bassoon, the 4th highest range center (sounding B♭1–G4); no octave shift, no repair
